title: Alice & Bob Accelerates Modular Cat-Qubit Roadmap to 200 Logical Qubits from 3,600 Physical Qubits by 2030 - Quantum Computing Report
author: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
text:
Paris- and Boston-based quantum computing company Alice & Bob has unveiled an updated fault-tolerant hardware roadmap that doubles its 2030 logical-qubit target, aiming to deliver 200 logical qubits from 3,600 physical cat qubits in its Carbon utility-scale system before scaling to 2,048 logical qubits by 2034. Because superconducting cat qubits autonomously suppress bit-flip errors at the hardware level, the architecture focuses error-correction overhead primarily on phase-flip errors, substantially reducing the physical-to-logical qubit ratio required for fault tolerance.

According to technical specifications released alongside the roadmap, the 2030 Carbon architecture will occupy a 350-square-meter footprint and connect nine dilution refrigerators via cryogenic coaxial cables capable of exchanging Bell pairs across separate chips without degrading quantum states. The system is engineered around degree-five qubit connectivity, a hybrid low-density parity-check (LDPC) and repetition error-correction code, a 10-microsecond clock speed, 10 million logical operations, and a target logical error rate of 10−7.

Alice & Bob noted that the accelerated schedule builds on hardware milestones achieved under France’s PROQCIMA program, where the company fabricated, assembled, and operated three independent quantum processors while demonstrating all core logical-qubit building blocks near the error-correction threshold. Combined with AI-assisted chip design and algorithmic optimizations that cut estimated RSA-2048 resource requirements by a factor of 40, the modular multi-cryostat design bypasses single-fridge scaling limits through standardized QPU manufacturing.
